first_decision: Whether the subject yields one independently acceptable outcome or several — the `single` vs `split` decomposition decision (Phase 2), taken before any block design; blocks cannot answer that question, and outcomes must be independently acceptable/handoffable without duplicating the same normative rules, not split by BE/FE, screens, teams or agent count. Here two potentially independent outcomes are only apparent, so `single` stands unless independent acceptance is proven.
composition_decision: article-led for every resulting article — fixed; there is no `article-first | hybrid` route choice.
authoring_order: A complete working pass through the unchanged template must exist first: each article's whole-template baseline draft is the starting deliverable, and semantic blocks are defined only afterwards as focused depth lenses, each block stage integrated into a new article projection (no final-only stitch).
next_gate: All three artifacts validated and presented with framing, recommendation, estimate range, trade-offs and the visible `simplicity-spec` result; every batched direct `user-decision` question asked and answered; the user's choice recorded so the decomposition decision and plan move from `proposed` to `approved` with the same `subject_id` and exact `decision_ref`. Only then may `caseflow.py init` initialize each specification. In this scenario the external write is unauthorized, so `external_sync` stays `not_requested` and no Singularity publication or read-back receipt is part of the gate; if it were separately authorized, `synced` would additionally require `system`, `target_ref` and `readback_ref`.
